newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrat set to sue China-appointed legislature.
newsitem.headline: HK democrat set to sue China-appointed legislature.

text.p: A leading Hong Kong politician said on Tuesday he would sue the legislature Beijing plans to install in the territory if it passes laws before the British colony is returned to China.

Controversy over the provisional legislature grew after Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen defended the interim chamber on Monday and signalled it would pass laws even before Britain hands back the territory on July 1.
Martin Lee, chairman of Hong Kong's Democratic Party, said his party would launch an immediate court challenge if the interim body approved legislation before the handover.
"We will act according to the provisional legislature's decision," Lee told reporters.
"There are two ways of challenging it. One way is for somebody to go to the court as soon as they have begun to purport to legislate," Lee said.
The other avenue was after the handover, when any person charged with an offence under a law passed by the provisional legislature before the flag change could file suit, Lee said.
The 60-member provisional chamber was chosen by a 400-strong Beijing-anointed caucus in December to replace Hong Kong's current elected Legislative Council.

Britain and Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp oppose the body, saying it breaks Hong Kong's constitution, which allows only one legislature to operate in the territory. They contend that if it passes laws, holds meetings, or opens offices in Hong Kong before July 1, it will be breaking the law.
But pro-China politician Chung Sze-yuen, who is close to Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa, told reporters the shadow legislature could pass laws before midnight on June 30.
The interim body has held meetings in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, just across the border, to avoid any legal challenge.
China has provoked jitters in the territory of 6.4 million with its plans to have the interim chamber roll back laws protecting civil liberties and democracy.
